name: Shakti 60-min bilateral session: amygdala signal (slow alternation)
summary: Murphy's single 60-minute Shakti session 'to try to create an intense experience in ONE session': his amygdala signal over both temporal lobes on the 8 Coil Shakti, switching between the two coil pairs after each burst (the vendor's standard mode). The one independent test of the Shakti amygdala signal used the fast mode, not this one, and found no effect (Gendle & McGrath 2012).
setting: Blindfold, earplugs or a sound-blocking headset (the vendor: 'substituting white noise won't work'), no interruptions and no plans afterwards. Murphy: 'For the first twenty minutes, not much happens.'
schedule: A one-off for a single intense experience, not a series (the vendor: repeating it 'might eventually elicit an unpleasant experience'); at most once every 3 weeks.
notes: The vendor describes a one-off 60-minute session that 'should be bilateral'; its standard, slow mode switches stereo channels 'after one instance of the signal' (pages on 60-minute sessions and the 8 Coil Shakti). It gives its amygdala signal only by name, 3-ms points and a latency of 'about four seconds'. The burst here is the project's rising sweep, 6 to 30 Hz, at the lab's burst length of 230 points (Ryczko 2002 p.1 [592], p.2 [593]), 0.69 s; no point values were published. Four coils sit over each temporal lobe: top C5/C6 with bottom T9/T10 as one pair per side, front FT7/FT8 with back TP7/TP8 as the other. One burst plays on the first pair of both sides and the next, 4.69 s later, on the second, so each pair gets a burst every 9.38 s. Each pair has one (+) and one (-) coil after the vendor's 'Getting started' chart; its photos give other signs. Site names are the project's reading. murphy-shakti-60min-bilateral-amygdala-fast has the twice-a-second mode. Field strength: the vendor's 10 to 50 mG are gaussmeter readings at a coil; Gendle & McGrath read 0.1 to 1.0 uT in the centre of the headpiece, 9 cm from the coils (p.11 [227]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT that is about 56 uT at the coil face, 11 to 56 times the vendor's level, and about 0.02 uT per coil at 9 cm. Gendle & McGrath 2012 tested the fast alternating amygdala signal, not this slow mode (p.4 [220]). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). In Gillis & Persinger 1993 aggression rose with 20 min of continuous field, not with the pattern given 1 s every 4 s, as here (4 per group, p.2 [169]). Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition; stop on distress.
